# Slate

> Slate is a calorie journal for iPhone, built for India, by Sonal Systems Private Limited (Vadodara, Gujarat). You type what you ate the way you'd say it, in English, Hinglish or Gujarati spellings ("2 roti aur ek katori dal"), and Slate puts a number next to it. No login. Data stored in Mumbai, India. Not related to Slate magazine (slate.com) or other products named Slate.

Slate is free forever. Slate Plus is optional: ₹399 a month or ₹2,999 a year in India (7 days free on yearly), $4.99 a month or $34.99 a year in the US, and £4.99 a month or £34.99 a year in the UK. It adds voice and photo logging, delivery orders, chat and more. iPhone only, iOS 18 or later. Coming soon to the App Store.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://writeonslate.com/): what Slate is, with a clickable demo of the app
- [About Slate and Sonal Systems](https://writeonslate.com/about/): Slate is a calorie journal for iPhone, built for Indian food by Sonal Systems Private Limited in Vadodara, Gujarat. Who makes it and how to reach us.
- [How Slate counts calories in Indian food](https://writeonslate.com/how-slate-counts/): How every number on Slate is worked out: textbook recipes in grams, IFCT 2017 values, cooked weights, katoris, outside ranges, cross-checks and rounding.
- [Privacy policy](https://writeonslate.com/privacy/)
- [Terms of use](https://writeonslate.com/terms/)
- [Support](https://writeonslate.com/support/): support@writeonslate.com

## Food calories

- [Calories in Indian food: roti, dal, rice and more](https://writeonslate.com/calories/): Calories, protein, carbs and fat for everyday Indian dishes, by katori, piece and plate, worked out from IFCT 2017 recipes in grams.
- [Indian meal calorie calculator: type what you ate](https://writeonslate.com/calories/calculator/): Type a meal the way you'd say it, in English or Hinglish, and get calories, protein, carbs and fat from home recipes and IFCT 2017. Free, in your browser.
- [Roti calories: 95 each, 140 with ghee, 190 for 2](https://writeonslate.com/calories/roti/): A medium roti made with 30 g of atta has about 95 calories. Phulka, chapati and roti with ghee, worked out from IFCT 2017.
- [Rice calories: 160 per katori, 120 per 100 g cooked](https://writeonslate.com/calories/plain-rice/): A 200 ml katori of plain cooked rice has about 160 calories. White rice by katori, plate and 100 g, worked out from IFCT 2017.
- [Dal tadka calories: 115 per katori, 275 with rice](https://writeonslate.com/calories/dal-tadka/): A 200 ml katori of thin dal tadka has about 115 calories; thick dal has up to about twice that. Toor dal with a ghee tadka, from IFCT 2017.
- [Rajma calories: 210 per katori, 370 with rice](https://writeonslate.com/calories/rajma/): A 200 ml katori of rajma curry has about 210 calories and 8 g protein. Home rajma, worked out from IFCT 2017.
- [Poha calories: 315 per plate, 155 a small bowl](https://writeonslate.com/calories/poha/): A plate of poha made with 40 g of dry poha has about 315 calories. Kanda and batata poha with peanuts, from IFCT 2017 and a textbook recipe.
- [Idli calories: 50 each, 305 for 2 with sambar](https://writeonslate.com/calories/idli/): One medium idli has about 50 calories, and 2 medium idlis about 105. Rice and urad dal idli, worked out from IFCT 2017.
- [Masala dosa calories: 255 each, 455 with sambar](https://writeonslate.com/calories/masala-dosa/): A home masala dosa has about 255 calories with a teaspoon of oil, or 335 with a tablespoon. From IFCT 2017 and a textbook recipe.
- [Samosa calories: 165 each, 335 for 2](https://writeonslate.com/calories/samosa/): A home aloo samosa has about 165 calories; a street samosa about 160 to 285. From IFCT 2017 and measured street samples.
- [Paneer butter masala calories: 300 per katori, 150 per 100 g](https://writeonslate.com/calories/paneer-butter-masala/): A 200 ml katori of home paneer butter masala has about 300 calories; a restaurant serving often has two or three times that. From IFCT 2017.
- [Masala chai calories: 60 a cup, 30 without sugar](https://writeonslate.com/calories/masala-chai/): A cup of masala chai with 50 ml toned milk and 2 tsp sugar has about 60 calories; without sugar, about 30. Worked out per cup.
- [Phulka calories: 75 each, 155 for 2, 120 with ghee](https://writeonslate.com/calories/phulka/): One phulka made with about 24 g of atta has about 75 calories, or 120 with a teaspoon of ghee. Counts for 2, 3 and 4 phulkas.
- [Plain paratha calories: 165 each, 210 with ghee](https://writeonslate.com/calories/plain-paratha/): A plain paratha made with 27 g of atta and 2 teaspoons of oil has about 165 calories. With ghee or butter on top, and dhaba sizes.
- [Aloo paratha calories: 190 each, 440 for 2 with curd](https://writeonslate.com/calories/aloo-paratha/): A homemade aloo paratha has about 190 calories, or 225 with a teaspoon of butter. Worked out from a textbook recipe and IFCT 2017.
- [Thepla calories: 120 each, 245 for 2, 365 for 3](https://writeonslate.com/calories/thepla/): One methi thepla has about 120 calories, so 3 theplas come to about 365. Worked out from a recipe in grams and IFCT 2017.
- [Puri calories: 95 each, 385 for 4, 570 with aloo sabzi](https://writeonslate.com/calories/puri/): A home puri made with 13 g of atta has about 95 calories once fried; 4 puris have about 385. Frying oil counted from lab data.
- [Bhatura calories: 185 each, 635 for 2 with chole](https://writeonslate.com/calories/bhatura/): A home bhatura made with 27 g of maida has about 185 calories once fried. Street bhaturas tested in a lab came to about 90 to 185.
- [Naan calories: 175 each, 525 for a large restaurant naan](https://writeonslate.com/calories/naan/): A home naan made with 40 g of maida has about 175 calories. A large 10-inch restaurant naan is about 525. Worked out from IFCT 2017.
- [Butter naan calories: 210 each, 595 restaurant size](https://writeonslate.com/calories/butter-naan/): A home butter naan with a teaspoon of butter has about 210 calories; a large restaurant one is about 420 to 630. From IFCT 2017.
- [Plain dosa calories: 145 each, 345 with sambar](https://writeonslate.com/calories/plain-dosa/): A plain dosa has about 145 calories with ¾ teaspoon of oil, and about 115 without. Sizes, ghee and restaurant dosas compared.

## Who Slate is for

- [Who Slate is for: Indian food, home cooking, eating out](https://writeonslate.com/for/): How to count calories in Indian food at home, at the office, eating out and on fasting days, in Hinglish, without a login. Written by the makers of Slate.
- [Calorie counter for Indian food: katori, roti and oil](https://writeonslate.com/for/indian-food/): Why calorie apps struggle with dal, roti and sabzi, what an honest number for Indian food needs, and how Slate counts by your katori, roti and oil.
- [Calorie counting for vegetarians, including Jain food](https://writeonslate.com/for/vegetarians/): Counting calories and protein in vegetarian and Jain meals: dal, paneer, curd, chana and besan, with katori-by-katori numbers from IFCT 2017.
- [Counting calories in home-cooked food: katori, roti, oil](https://writeonslate.com/for/home-cooking/): Three things decide the calories in home-cooked Indian food: your katori, your roti and your oil. How to measure each once, with numbers from IFCT 2017.
- [Calories in restaurant, Swiggy and Zomato food](https://writeonslate.com/for/eating-out/): Why restaurant and delivery food has more calories than home food, with ranges for dal makhani, paneer, biryani and naan, and how to count an order.
- [A calorie tracker you can write in Hinglish](https://writeonslate.com/for/hinglish/): Write "2 roti aur ek katori dal" or "chai, kam cheeni" and get a number. How Slate reads Hinglish and Gujarati spellings, and what it does when it can't.
- [A calorie tracker without login or ads](https://writeonslate.com/for/no-login/): Slate has no login, no ads and no tracking. What it stores, where (Mumbai, India), what it never collects, and how to export or delete everything.
- [Calories on fasting days: Navratri, Ekadashi, Ramadan](https://writeonslate.com/for/fasting/): Fasting-day food like sabudana khichdi, kuttu puri and iftar snacks often has more calories than it looks. How to count it, with IFCT 2017 numbers.
- [Calories in office canteen food and tiffin](https://writeonslate.com/for/office-canteen-tiffin/): How to count a canteen thali, a tiffin dabba and office chai: rotis, katoris of dal and sabzi, and the extra oil in canteen cooking, from IFCT 2017.

## Blog

- [Blog: counting calories in Indian food](https://writeonslate.com/blog/): Articles on counting calories in Indian food: katori sizes, home and restaurant dal, chai, thalis, fasting days and maintenance calories.
- [Why your katori size changes your calorie count](https://writeonslate.com/blog/katori-size-calories/): A 250 ml katori holds two thirds more than a 150 ml one. How katori size changes the calories in dal, rice and sabzi, and how to measure yours.
- [Home dal vs restaurant dal: where the calories come from](https://writeonslate.com/blog/home-dal-vs-restaurant-dal/): Why a katori of restaurant dal can have twice the calories of home dal: thickness, ghee, butter, cream and portion size, with numbers from IFCT 2017.
- [Your chai over a day: what 3 or 4 cups add up to](https://writeonslate.com/blog/chai-calories/): Four cups of chai a day with 2 teaspoons of sugar each come to about 245 calories. What 2, 3, 4 and 5 cups add up to, with and without sugar.
- [How to count calories in a thali without weighing anything](https://writeonslate.com/blog/count-thali-calories/): Count a thali by its pieces and katoris: rotis, dal, rice, sabzi, farsan and sweets. Worked examples for a Gujarati, a Punjabi and a South Indian thali.
- [Counting calories on fasting days without stress](https://writeonslate.com/blog/fasting-day-calories/): Navratri, Ekadashi and Ramadan food is often more filling in calories than it looks. A calm way to count it, and when it's fine not to count at all.
- [What "maintenance calories" means, and how to measure yours](https://writeonslate.com/blog/maintenance-calories/): Maintenance calories are what your body uses in a day. How formulas estimate it, why they're only a starting point, and how to measure yours from a log.
- [Diwali sweets: calories per piece, from kaju katli to kheer](https://writeonslate.com/blog/diwali-sweets-calories/): Calories in one piece of every common Diwali sweet: kaju katli 50, soan papdi 105, motichoor ladoo 115, gulab jamun 155, and the snacks.

## Facts

- Numbers are worked out from the Indian Food Composition Tables (IFCT 2017) and adjusted for your kitchen.
- AI only reads lines Slate doesn't recognise, spots dishes in photos, and powers chat. It never produces a calorie number. Your Slate isn't used to train AI models.
- Not medical advice. For anyone 18 or older.
